key_insight: AI-generated handoffs matched clinician handoffs on overall quality, but traded greater completeness and organization for less conciseness and accuracy.
clinical_relevance: AI may reduce handoff documentation burden in hospital medicine, but its different error patterns mean clinician oversight remains important before workflow adoption.
method: Retrospective comparison of AI-generated vs clinician-authored end-of-rotation handoffs
Large language model tool built using clinical notes from the electronic health record
Structured review assessed quality and safety domains
evidence_signal: Overall quality scores were similar (3.7 vs 3.5, p=0.57), with comparable error rates (0.3 per handoff in both groups) but different error types.
watch_item: AI handoffs included inaccuracies and hallucinations, so prospective testing in real clinical workflows is still needed.
paper_title: Quality and Safety profiles of AI-Generated vs Clinician-Generated Handoffs in Hospital Medicine
